## Proof

Let $x = \omega$ (a primitive cube root of unity, so $\omega^2+\omega+1=0$, $\omega^3=1$, $\omega\neq 1$) and $y = \sqrt[3]{2}$ (so $y^3=2$). We determine $\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\omega,\sqrt[3]{2})/\mathbb{Q})$.

### Step 1. The field is the splitting field of $t^3-2$

The roots of $t^3-2$ are $\sqrt[3]{2},\ \omega\sqrt[3]{2},\ \omega^2\sqrt[3]{2}$, all lying in $\mathbb{Q}(\omega,\sqrt[3]{2})$. Hence $\mathbb{Q}(\omega,\sqrt[3]{2})$ is the splitting field of the separable polynomial $t^3-2$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and is therefore a Galois extension of $\mathbb{Q}$.

### Step 2. Degree of the extension

- $[\mathbb{Q}(\omega):\mathbb{Q}]=2$, since $\omega$ has minimal polynomial $t^2+t+1$ (irreducible, no rational roots).
- $[\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[3]{2}):\mathbb{Q}]=3$, since $\sqrt[3]{2}$ has minimal polynomial $t^3-2$ (irreducible by Eisenstein at $p=2$).
- The degrees $2$ and $3$ are coprime, so $\mathbb{Q}(\omega)\cap\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[3]{2})=\mathbb{Q}$.

Therefore
$$[\mathbb{Q}(\omega,\sqrt[3]{2}):\mathbb{Q}] = 2\cdot 3 = 6,$$
and $|\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\omega,\sqrt[3]{2})/\mathbb{Q})|=6$.

### Step 3. Description of the automorphisms

Any $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\omega,\sqrt[3]{2})/\mathbb{Q})$ is determined by its values on the two generators, and must send each to a conjugate root:
- $\sigma(\omega)\in\{\omega,\omega^2\}$ (roots of $t^2+t+1$),
- $\sigma(\sqrt[3]{2})\in\{\sqrt[3]{2},\omega\sqrt[3]{2},\omega^2\sqrt[3]{2}\}$ (roots of $t^3-2$).

This gives $2\times 3=6$ automorphisms, confirming the order. Define two generators:

- $\rho:\ \sqrt[3]{2}\mapsto\omega\sqrt[3]{2},\quad \omega\mapsto\omega$ (rotation),
- $\tau:\ \sqrt[3]{2}\mapsto\sqrt[3]{2},\quad \omega\mapsto\omega^2$ (complex conjugation).

### Step 4. Orders and the defining relation

**$\rho$ has order 3:**
$$\rho^2(\sqrt[3]{2})=\omega^2\sqrt[3]{2},\qquad \rho^3(\sqrt[3]{2})=\omega^3\sqrt[3]{2}=\sqrt[3]{2},$$
and $\rho$ fixes $\omega$, so $\rho^3=\mathrm{id}$, with $\rho\neq\mathrm{id},\rho^2\neq\mathrm{id}$.

**$\tau$ has order 2:**
$$\tau^2(\omega)=\tau(\omega^2)=(\omega^2)^2=\omega^4=\omega,\qquad \tau^2(\sqrt[3]{2})=\sqrt[3]{2},$$
so $\tau^2=\mathrm{id}$, $\tau\neq\mathrm{id}$.

**Conjugation relation** $\tau\rho\tau^{-1}=\rho^{-1}$ (using $\tau^{-1}=\tau$):
$$\tau\rho\tau(\sqrt[3]{2})=\tau\rho(\sqrt[3]{2})=\tau(\omega\sqrt[3]{2})=\omega^2\sqrt[3]{2}=\rho^2(\sqrt[3]{2})=\rho^{-1}(\sqrt[3]{2}),$$
$$\tau\rho\tau(\omega)=\tau\rho(\omega^2)=\tau(\omega^2)=\omega^4=\omega=\rho^{-1}(\omega).$$
Hence $\tau\rho\tau=\rho^{-1}$.

### Step 5. The group is non-abelian, hence $S_3$

The group is non-abelian:
$$\rho\tau(\sqrt[3]{2})=\rho(\sqrt[3]{2})=\omega\sqrt[3]{2},\qquad \tau\rho(\sqrt[3]{2})=\tau(\omega\sqrt[3]{2})=\omega^2\sqrt[3]{2},$$
so $\rho\tau\neq\tau\rho$.

There are exactly two groups of order $6$: the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_6$ (abelian) and the symmetric group $S_3\cong D_3$ (non-abelian). Since our group is non-abelian, it must be $S_3$.

Concretely, the presentation
$$\langle \rho,\tau \mid \rho^3=\tau^2=\mathrm{id},\ \tau\rho\tau=\rho^{-1}\rangle$$
is the standard presentation of the dihedral group $D_3\cong S_3$. The six elements $\{\mathrm{id},\rho,\rho^2,\tau,\rho\tau,\rho^2\tau\}$ correspond to the six permutations of the three roots $\{\sqrt[3]{2},\omega\sqrt[3]{2},\omega^2\sqrt[3]{2}\}$, giving an explicit isomorphism onto $S_3$.

### Conclusion

$$\boxed{\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\omega,\sqrt[3]{2})/\mathbb{Q})\cong S_3\cong D_3}$$

the symmetric group on three letters (equivalently, the dihedral group of order $6$).
